name: V2.1 Research-Optimized Recomposition + Boxing
description: A 12-week, seven-day body-recomposition program prioritizing shoulders, upper back, chest, arms, balanced legs, visible abs, boxing skill, aerobic fitness, and symptom-free movement control. Home and gym choices are alternatives within each slot, not extra exercises.
goals: Wider, rounder shoulders and a stronger shoulder-to-waist ratio
A thicker upper back, stronger chest, and larger arms
Visible abs and a gradually smaller waist without bulking
Better boxing skill, conditioning, and aerobic fitness
Neck, scapular, thoracic, and rib-pelvis movement control
Maintain or increase strength during gradual fat loss
Support metabolic health, recovery, and male fertility with sustainable training

effort: Most compound movements: finish with 1-3 clean repetitions in reserve.
Most accessory movements: finish with 1-2 repetitions in reserve.
Only selected isolation final sets may approach 0-1 RIR during harder blocks.
Do not repeatedly train compound movements to failure; clean form takes priority over the rep target.
progression: Use double progression: begin near the lower or middle part of the rep range and keep the load while adding clean reps.
Increase load by the smallest practical increment only after every planned work set reaches the top of the range at the required RIR.
After increasing load, return toward the lower part of the rep range.
Track every exercise variation independently; do not compare loads between home, cable, machine, Smith, or free-weight variations.
Keep a main variation stable for roughly one four-week block when practical.
rest: Most presses and rows: rest 90-150 seconds.
Posture and control work: rest 30-60 seconds.
Rest longer when needed to preserve repetitions and technique.
substitutions: Choose one exercise from each slot; Home and Gym alternatives are not performed together.
Substitute for equipment availability, discomfort, training location, stalled progression, or safety.
Keep each variation's performance history separate.
rules.postureCue: Use comfortable symptom-free positions. Keep the chin controlled, let the scapulae move naturally, and avoid borrowing range through neck extension or excessive lower-back arching.
returnAfterBreak: Less than about 7 days away: normally resume V2.1 without the special workout.
About 7-13 days away: complete one Full-Body Re-entry, take one recovery day, then restart Day 1.
About 14-28+ days away: complete one Full-Body Re-entry, take one or two recovery days, then restart Day 1.
During the first normal week after 14-28+ days away, reduce strength-training set volume about 20-30% and stay near 3 RIR.
Do not compensate for missed sessions or immediately test previous maximum strength.
optionalNeckWork: Only if completely symptom-free, use easy-to-moderate four-way neck isometrics no more than twice per week.
Use 2 sets of 10-20 seconds per direction; never use maximal effort or a heavy neck harness.
safety: Do not claim exercise changes spinal structure; train strength, movement control, scapular function, thoracic mobility, and rib-pelvis positioning.
Stop rather than push through sharp or radiating pain, numbness, new weakness, grip weakness, significant unusual joint pain, severe or persistent neck/back pain, dizziness, or neurological symptoms.
Press without jutting the chin or gaining range through excessive lumbar arching; pull with the arms and scapulae rather than neck extension.
Stop hinges before lumbar control changes, use only pain-free dip depth, and put boxing mechanics before maximal power.
Do not use anabolic steroids, exogenous testosterone, hormonal test boosters, crash dieting, or chronic extreme exercise.

coaching.fastLossGuidance: If loss exceeds about 0.5 kg/week while performance and recovery worsen, consider adding about 100-150 kcal/day.
healthContext: Use actual body-weight, waist, performance, and recovery trends rather than a permanently hardcoded calorie target.
Favor whole foods, adequate nutrition, sleep, aerobic fitness, and moderate sustainable fat loss while trying to conceive.

standaloneWorkouts.name: Full-Body Re-entry
standaloneWorkouts.description: A gentle whole-body technical re-exposure after a significant break from resistance training. It provides a full-body stimulus with low-to-moderate fatigue before restarting Day 1.
standaloneWorkouts.recommendedUse: Use this after a significant training break before restarting Day 1. About 7-13 days away: take one recovery day afterward. About 14-28+ days away: take one or two recovery days afterward and reduce first-week strength volume about 20-30% at roughly 3 RIR.
rules: Use about 3 RIR on every set and never train to failure.
If reliable prior data exists, 60-70% of the previously expected working load may be a reference, but never force a percentage; choose a clearly manageable load.
No 1RM tests, PR attempts, forced reps, drop sets, maximal weighted pull-ups or dips, or grinder reps.
The optional finisher is easy technique or walking only; no HIIT, maximal rounds, sprints, AMRAPs, or exhaustion training.
Take at least one recovery day afterward; take two if significant soreness or fatigue remains, then restart normal V2.1 at Day 1.
